docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
Before cybersecurity, I served as a U.S. Army Green Beret specializing in communications, deploying radio and satellite systems in austere environments. That work taught me how critical it is to keep communications reliable and secure under pressure.

That experience led me to pursue an Associate of Applied Science (AAS) in Computer Information Technology with a Local Area Network Systems – Cybersecurity Specialization. I quickly found I had a knack for the concepts, and I'm now building hands-on skills through CTFs, labs, and networking studies.

docs.title: CTF Reflection
docs.text:
Competing in CTFs was one of the most rewarding parts of my training. The scenarios put classroom concepts into real-world practice, which made them stick in a way lectures alone can't. Hands-on challenges brought the theory to life and gave me a taste of what real security work feels like.

CTFs also showed me exactly where I need to grow. Identifying the areas I struggled with gave me a clear focus for further study. Most importantly, I learned there's rarely one "right" way to solve a problem. Every challenge can be approached creatively, and each new approach teaches me something new.

docs.title: NCL Performance (Fall 2026)
docs.text:
• Individual Game: 698th of 5,961 (89th percentile), 92.1% accuracy. Top categories: Network Traffic Analysis and Forensics (98th percentile), OSINT (94th percentile). View report
  • Team Game (SANS.edu Phantom Packets): 205th of 3,034 (94th percentile), 2,530 of 3,000 points. Top categories: Forensics (99th percentile), Network Traffic Analysis and Scanning & Reconnaissance (96th percentile). View report

docs.title: Highlight: AI-Assisted Security Automation
docs.text: One of my favorite projects has been integrating an AI agent with a custom MCP (Model Context Protocol) server written in Python. The server lets the agent parse and analyze logs, so I can automate repetitive security tasks and focus on the investigation itself. It's been a fun way to combine scripting, AI, and security, and the possibilities are as wide as my creativity.
